name: Duo Synth
explanation: A duophonic analog lead/bass synthesizer modelled feature-for-feature on the ARP Odyssey (Owner's Manual, Second Edition, March 1976). The keyboard is 2-voice paraphonic: the lowest held key drives VCO 1 (low-note priority) and the highest held key drives VCO 2 (high-note priority), exactly as the specifications state, so two keys sound as two distinct pitches while a single key locks both oscillators together. Two VCOs each offer sawtooth or square/pulse with a variable PULSE WIDTH (50%->5%) and PULSE-WIDTH MODULATION; VCO 1 has a low-frequency (LF) mode; VCO 2 has hard SYNC to VCO 1. The signature ARP modulation matrix is a set of amount sliders each fed by a two-position source switch: VCO1+2 FM (Sine-LFO / S&H), VCO2 FM (Sine-LFO / ADSR), VCO1 PWM and VCO2 PWM (Sine-LFO / ADSR), VCF FM x2 (Sine-LFO / S&H and ADSR / AR) and VCF keyboard tracking (Kbd / S&H). Sources: a LOW FREQUENCY OSCILLATOR with simultaneous sine and square outputs, a SAMPLE & HOLD (its own 2-input mixer, LFO- or keyboard-clocked, with output LAG) and the two envelopes. AUDIO MIXER blends VCO1, VCO2 and a third channel switchable between white/pink NOISE and the RING MODULATOR (VCO1xVCO2). The self-oscillating 4-pole low-pass VCF (Q to 30, resonance to self-oscillation) is preceded by a non-resonant HIGH-PASS FILTER. The VCA is driven by the ADSR, the AR or a straight GATE (drone), with an initial-GAIN slider. Performance: PORTAMENTO, master TUNE, +/-2-octave TRANSPOSE, +/-1-octave PITCH BEND with centre dead-zone, PPC vibrato depth, a REPEAT switch (Kbd gate / Auto-repeat / Kbd-repeat that lets the LFO retrigger the envelopes) and VOLUME. Switch groups are bit-packed into two mask parameters so the whole instrument fits the 64-param host pool; the panel decodes every individual switch.
